wiki: Black Mesa Wiki (https://black-mesa-source.fandom.com/api.php), the Fandom wiki about the Black Mesa game itself; and the Half-Life Wiki (https://half-life.fandom.com/api.php), its page 'Black Mesa (game)' only. No Combine OverWiki page is used: its 29 saved pages describe the 1998 game and say nothing about the remake.

licence_stored: CC-BY-SA-3.0 (the fetcher prints 'CC-BY-SA' with no version; the library stores the versioned form, as it does for its other Fandom wikis)
how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py --api <the wiki's api.php> --titles <pages> --out build/wiki-live/<wiki> (page text as rendered by the wiki, link markup removed; saved under build/wiki-live/black-mesa-source/ and build/wiki-live/half-life-fandom/). Every quoted sentence below was checked, by script, to appear word for word (spaces collapsed) in the saved page text at the revision named. Each line was written from a short list of facts, not from the page's sentence. Every quote sits in the wiki editors' own prose, in an editors' bullet list of differences, or in an infobox table; the 'sits_in' field of each quote says which. None sits in a quote block, a description box, an attribution line or a trophy, codex or booklet entry. The Black Mesa Wiki's 'Comparisons' page lists, per creature and weapon, how Black Mesa differs from the 1998 Half-Life; the notes use only lines it or the Half-Life Wiki's 'Black Mesa (game)' page say of Black Mesa. Lines that name the free 2012 version only are not used, except where they say the Steam version differs.

lines.line: Summary: A big armoured Xen soldier with 120 health. On Earth it fires hornets in rapid bursts and then charges in; on Xen it is more agile and can jump onto platforms.

drawn_from.sits_in: bare fact from the page's infobox table
quoted: !! Health: || 120

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Alien Grunts are large bipedal alien from Xen

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: In the Earthbound chapters, their AI is to shoot hornets rapidly and charge, later in the Xen chapters, their AI appears to be more agile and they can jump onto platforms.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: It should be noted that Alien Grunts are more agile in Xen than they were on Earth, being able to strafe faster and jump towards elevated surfaces.

lines.line: Weak points: The unarmoured part of its torso: one crossbow bolt kills it there, even on Hard.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: being capable of killing an Alien Grunt with one hit in the unarmored part of the torso, even in Hard mode

lines.line: Looks like: Large and stocky, with a small extra arm on its chest. It stands more upright and wears more armour than the 1998 original.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Alien Grunts are large bipedal alien from Xen, sporting stocky builds and the classic vestigial chest-arm.
They both stand further upright and sport more armor than their cousins in Half-Life

lines.line: Tips: Its hornets do not home in on you. A hornet hit does 9 damage and a punch 30. The kind with no armour and no Hivehand has none to fire and simply charges at you.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: However, the hornets aren't homing towards the player.
The Unarmored without a Hivehand variant is the Alien Grunt that was released from its tube. The unarmored will just charge at you.

drawn_from.sits_in: bare fact from the page's infobox table
quoted: - Melee: 30
- Hornet: 9

lines.line: Summary: A small parasite about the size of a person's head that leaps up to 3 metres (10 feet) at its target. It is the first enemy you meet.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Headcrabs are nonsentient parasitic aliens originating from Xen.
Headcrab is the first enemy you encounter in-game.
Headcrabs are roughly the size of an adult human head.
enough jumping power to leap up to 3 meters (10ft) into any direction

lines.line: Weak points: One crowbar hit or two Glock 17 shots kill it on every difficulty. After a missed leap it is in a bad position and turns round very slowly or tries to retreat.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: the headcrab will be put in a bad position, requiring it to turn around at a very slow speed or attempt to retreat.
on all difficulties, they can be killed with one Crowbar hit or two shots from a Glock 17.

lines.line: Looks like: Smooth-skinned, with four short, strong legs. Its look is closer to the Half-Life 2 headcrab than to the 1998 one.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Their bodies are covered by smooth skin, and have four short and powerful legs

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Both the Headcrab's and Vortigaunt's models look closer to their appearances in Half-Life 2.

lines.line: Tips: Some burrow into the ground and come out as you walk up, and its small size makes it hard to hit. Heavy props kill it, it drowns in water, and a flare sets it alight.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: One of their main advantages is their small size, making them a difficult target along with the capability of burrowing into the ground and getting out as soon as the target approaches.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: It can be killed/gibbed with heavy props.
Can drown from water.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: in Black Mesa, they can be used to burn Zombies and Headcrabs.

lines.line: Summary: People taken over by headcrabs. They only fight up close, clawing for 20 damage a hit, and have 50 health. They come as scientists, guards and marines, plus a tougher suited kind.

drawn_from.sits_in: bare fact from the page's infobox table
quoted: || Damage per hit || 20.
|| Health || 50.
|| Weapons || Claws.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: being regular humans with Headcrabs latched onto their head
They only attack by clawing at their foes, making them only close-quarters threats

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The Headcrab zombie will have 4 different variants such as the scientist zombie, the guard zombie, the marine zombie, and lastly, an armored H.E.V zombie .

lines.line: Weak points: The suited kind is much tougher than the rest, and its head is the only part its suit does not cover.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Due to the HEV's resistance, ZEVs are much more durable than the average zombie, leaving only their heads unprotected.

lines.line: Looks like: A person with a headcrab on the head and a body that is rotting open. Some are torsos that crawl; the suited kind wears an HEV suit.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: causing their body to decompose and reveal internal organs

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The Headcrab zombie will have torso-only variants similar to Half-Life 2.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: ZEVs — Zombified scientists wearing HEV Suits

lines.line: Tips: They can punch props and objects so that they fly at you. Shots to some body parts stagger them, and a shot from chest to foot can leave the headcrab alive to leave its host. A flare sets them alight.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: can punch props and other objects causing them to fly towards their targets and partially wound them.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The Headcrab zombie can be staggered when shot in specific parts of the host's body.
When shooting the Headcrab zombies in the chest to foot, the Headcrab can survive and leave the host.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: in Black Mesa, they can be used to burn Zombies and Headcrabs.

lines.line: Summary: An alien that dodges when you aim at it and uses a shockwave when you get close.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The Vortigaunt will dodge when the player aims at them.
The Vortigaunt will use a shockwave when the player is near them.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Vorts will use their uninterruptible ground slam attack, that kills any snarks instantly

lines.line: Looks like: Bent forward, with snail-like skin, a small extra arm on the chest and green rings round the neck and arms, like chains.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: they are bent forward, with snail like skin color and texture, with a vestigial arm on their chest, they have green rings and bands around their necks and arms similar to chains, or bonds.

lines.line: Tips: On Earth they are always hostile. In the Xen chapters they leave you alone, even if you provoke them, until an Alien Controller takes over their minds; they calm down again when it dies. Their ground slam kills snarks instantly.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: In the Earthbound chapters, they will be always hostile to the player.
But they will be hostile, once the Alien Controllers control their minds to attack Gordon Freeman.
Provoking the Vortiguants in the Xen cahpters will not elicit a response

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Unlike in the original, the Vortigaunts will immediately resume their passive behavior when the Alien Controllers are killed.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Vorts will use their uninterruptible ground slam attack, that kills any snarks instantly

lines.line: Summary: A creature that hangs from the ceiling and pulls up the props and people it grabs with its tongue. It has more health than in the 1998 game.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: appears in various levels on the roof of these levels.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: Grab up props.
Slowly descends the tongue after consuming 1 NPC.
Constricting the NPC when getting grabbed.
The Barnacle's health is increased thus making the Crowbar hit it 3 times instead of 1.

lines.line: Tips: It takes three crowbar hits instead of one. Whatever it grabs is squeezed, so a victim cannot survive being freed. On Xen an underwater kind hangs upside down from the bottom; only the crowbar, Glock 17, crossbow, RPG, Hivehand and explosives kill it. One achievement is about a barnacle eating a headcrab ten times.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The Barnacle's health is increased thus making the Crowbar hit it 3 times instead of 1.
(This prevents the NPC from surviving getting freed)
In the Xen chapters, the Barnacle also has its underwater counterpart, called Underwater Barnacle.
All of your weapons except the Crowbar, Glock-17, Crossbow, RPG, Hivehand, and explosives will be useless to kill this Barnacle.
There is an achievement that relates to a Barnacle devouring a Headcrab 10 times.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Beneathicles — Underwater Barnacles attached upside down at the bottom of the water that work like normal Barnacles.

lines.line: Summary: A spitting alien predator that stays calm until you come into its sight.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The Bullsquid is always calm when the player is out of sight of it.
The Bullsquid's acidic spit has more acidic spit than the original.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: more suited for being an aquatic predator

lines.line: Looks like: Its eyes sit on the top of its head, like a water hunter's.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Bullsquids have their eyes moved to the top of their head, more suited for being an aquatic predator.

lines.line: Tips: Its acid makes your suit warn of hazardous chemicals. Spit that lands in water slows down and stops, and touching a broken-up blob does no damage.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game); the bullet names the suit's spoken warning, which the note states in its own words and does not copy
quoted: The acidic spit will trigger the H.E.V to say "Warning, hazardous chemicals detected"
If the acidic spit has reached to water, it will move slowly and stop eventually. Trying to touch a frozen/broken acidic spit will not inflict damage.

lines.line: Summary: An alien that throws clusters of energy balls, dodges when you aim at it and can take over Vortigaunts' minds.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: Their secondary attack is changed to a cluster bomb type energy balls.
Can dodge when the player is aiming at it.
Can mind control Vortigaunts.

lines.line: Looks like: Redesigned since the 1998 game, mostly in its glow, which shows orange while it lifts objects.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: Their appearance is changed, especially their glow.
Can levitate objects, can be noticeable by emitting an orange glow.

lines.line: Tips: It teleports in when an alarm sounds. Crystals around it act as armour. Kill it and the Vortigaunts it controlled stop attacking.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: Can teleport in when an alarm sounds to control the situation.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: Alien Controllers will have crystals that they will use for armor.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Unlike in the original, the Vortigaunts will immediately resume their passive behavior when the Alien Controllers are killed.

lines.line: Summary: Female Black Ops assassins fight with a Glock 17 in each hand and do not throw grenades.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The Female Assassin equips an Akimbo of Glock-17s.
The Female Assassin's ability to throw grenades is removed.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: They also wield dual Glock 17 pistols (as opposed to a single one like the original game)

lines.line: Looks like: Black boots that look like Portal's long-fall boots, and pistols with no visible suppressor.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: now wearing what appear to be black Advanced Knee Replacements or Long Fall Boots from the Portal series.
while they don't have visible suppressors, the sound effects indicate otherwise.

lines.line: Tips: The pistols look unsuppressed but sound silenced. Their boots keep them from being hurt by falls. In the rooms where they wait they go hunting even if they have not seen you, then surround you, and there are more of them than in the 1998 game.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The Glock-17s are not equipped with suppressors, even though it uses a silenced version of the firing sound.
The Female Assassin also has Long Fall Boots equipped to save them from falling

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: Even if the assassins didn't see you, their AI will automatically set into hunting mode.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: All of the assassins except 1 will hunt you and surround you when arriving at the storage area. There will be more assassins than the original.

lines.line: Summary: A thrown beetle-like creature. Once released it chases enemies and bursts in a cloud of acidic blood about 3 metres across.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: exploding from overpressure, spraying chitin and acidic hemolymph fluid within a 3 meter radius.
Snarks are small, beetle-like xenian creatures

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: once chirps intensify, they'll move to explode in localized clouds of acidic blood and snark parts

lines.line: Uses: Their damage is all explosive, so armour does not reduce it, and a swarm can tear apart Alien Grunts and armoured vehicles. Five easily beat a marine squad; ten to fifteen suit bigger fights.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: since their damage this time around is 100% explosive, they're capable of ripping alien grunts, HECU armored vehicles
their armor bonuses don't count against explosives
A swarm of 5 will easily defeat an HECU squad, but it might be wiser to wait for bigger battles to unleash 10 or 15 of them at once.

lines.line: Tips: Ammo is scarce: under 70 snarks in the whole game, 5 from each nest and 15 carried at most. Unlike the original you can lob them gently or throw them across a room, and drop them. A Vortigaunt's ground slam kills them instantly, so deal with the Vortigaunts first. Their chirps show how much fight they have left.

drawn_from.sits_in: bare fact from the page's infobox table
quoted: !! Capacity: || 5 per nest/15 max capacity.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: with less than 70 snarks total in the vanilla game
Unlike in the original game, you're able to both lightly toss them or throw them across the room.

Vorts will use their uninterruptible ground slam attack, that kills any snarks instantly, so don't use them against xenian formations that include vorts unless you can eliminate the vorts before deploying the snarks.
Upon tossing them, snarks will emit chirps to tell you how much berserker juice they've left in the tank

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: Similar to the grenade it can be thrown away or dropped.

lines.line: Summary: A hard-hitting, slow-firing bolt gun that carries few bolts.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: the Crossbow deals extremely high damage
at the expense of a very low fire rate and much fewer bolts in reserve.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: even if you have something silent like the Crossbow

lines.line: Tips: The fire rate is very low, so make each bolt count; you carry at most 10. Bolts no longer ricochet in the Steam release. It is one of the few weapons that kill the underwater barnacle.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: at the expense of a very low fire rate and much fewer bolts in reserve.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Weapons and Items > Black Mesa Crossbow
drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)

lines.line: Summary: A flare you can pick up and use as a weapon: it sets enemies on fire.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: Flares can sometimes be picked up, allowing Gordon to set enemies on fire

lines.line: Uses: Burns zombies and headcrabs. Early on, before you find the crowbar, it is how you fend off the zombies.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: in Black Mesa, they can be used to burn Zombies and Headcrabs.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own prose
quoted: most notably early in the game when he hasn't picked up the crowbar yet and has to fend off zombies.

lines.line: Tips: Fire spreads when there is an exposed gas leak, so keep clear. Flares turn up in labs, and they also mark where a supply cache is close.

drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The flare can spread fire when there's an exposed gas leak.
Flares are commonly found in labs.
Flares are used to signal where the supply cache is nearby.

lines.line: Summary: A health pickup in two sizes: blue gives 10 health and is common, green gives 25 and is rare.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Weapons and Items > First Aid Kit
drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: There are 2 variants of the First Aid Kit.
The blue variant gives you +10 health. These are found commonly throughout Black Mesa.
The green variant gives you +25 health. These are found rarely throughout Black Mesa.

lines.line: Uses: Restores health: 10 from a blue kit, 25 from a green one.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Weapons and Items > First Aid Kit
drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The blue variant gives you +10 health.
The green variant gives you +25 health.

lines.line: Tips: Marine medics can drop a kit when killed, and green ones less often than blue. A wall First Aid Station is a separate refill: its tubes and lights show how much is left, and it closes when empty.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Weapons and Items > First Aid Kit
drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: H.E.C.U. Medics can drop these if dead.
H.E.C.U. Medics may drop them at a lower chance.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Weapons and Items > First Aid Station
drawn_from.sits_in: wiki editors' own bullet list (a list of differences from the 1998 game)
quoted: The First Aid Station has more details, with tubes with some healing juice to see how much is left, led lights to indicate if it's almost drained out.
